releases.name: Nightly 2026-10-23
releases.body:
Built from 0b9ecc2e on 2026-10-23.

Unreleased code — use a tagged release unless you are testing something specific.

Download with: gh release download nightly

Big stores are cheap to keep up to date. A pass that replaces a few sessions
appends their records instead of writing the whole log again and reads only
what changed: on a 40,000-session store 20 rewritten transcripts take 1.7 s
instead of 24 s, and peak memory drops from 7 GB to under 1 GB. A search for a
word most sessions hold answers in about a second instead of 24. Text taken
out of a transcript leaves the index on the next pass. For busy machines there
are `DEJA_NO_AUTO_INDEX` and `DEJA_SEARCH_ONLY`, and `deja index` exits 3 on a
partial run. Sub-agents are sessions of their own in every reader that marks
one, forks no longer take credit for what they copied, and recalled history
can no longer run a command in opencode or end a dsh turn. The index is rebuilt
once on upgrade.

A search for a word most sessions hold no longer reads all of them to show a page. Past 1,000 matches it ranks them first from the postings and the manifest, then reads the 1,000 that can reach the page and 200 more that check its length estimate; the total still counts every match, and `--all` scores every one as before. On a 40,000-session store a word in every session takes 1.1 s and 370 MB instead of 24 s and 2.6 GB, and MCP `recall` 2.5 s instead of 30 s (#5467).

The first index pass after a full build that rewrites, deletes or renames transcripts no longer reads the whole record log for the command-failure table: on a 40,000-session store, 20 rewritten transcripts take 4.0 s instead of 21 s, and the build leaves the table's state for that pass to start from (#5465). Renaming a transcript that shares its session with another file reads the session again only when the rename moves it past another of its files; 20 renames on the same store take 3.2 s instead of 20 s (#5466).
`deja --re` anchors `^` and `$` at each line, as grep does. They anchored the whole message, so `^panic:` missed a panic printed after any other tool output (#5448).
`deja embed` no longer sends a whole Cursor, Continue or Cline session again each time it grows. Those harnesses date unstamped turns from the file's modification time, and the vector identity held the time; it now holds only the session, role and text, so a session grown by one exchange embeds 2 records instead of every one. A version 2 sidecar is rekeyed on the next run without embedding again (#4976).

A search excerpt keeps the line that matched when it looks like tool noise. Searching `assignment to entry in nil map` showed the stack frames of a Go test panic and dropped the `panic:` line itself; `panic:`, `goroutine N`, `npm ERR!` and numbered lines are still left out when they do not hold the match (#5456). A `--re` search that finds nothing suggests a looser pattern, dropping `^`/`$`, or plain words, instead of "try fewer words or --re" (#5457).

`deja sync import` also leaves out a peer's records for a store `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES` (or a `harness:` line) excludes and for a project the policy `ignore` rule covers, and says how many; a relay no longer sends an excluded store's sessions on (#5435). The `sync-timer` unit carries the `DEJA_*` and `XDG_*` settings of the shell it was installed from, so a timer run syncs into the same index under the same switches (#5436).

A dsh turn no longer fails when recalled history contains `{{...}}`. dsh read deja's project digest and recall as prompt templates, so a past session quoting `{{cwd}}` ended every new turn with `unknown prompt variable` before the model was called; both contexts now pass `interpolate: false` and split the braces (`{ {cwd} }`), which dsh before 0.2.1-alpha.2 needs, in the npm plugin and in `deja install dsh-auto` (#5421).
`deja sync` holds a peer's records to this machine's switches: `DEJA_INDEX_TOOL_OUTPUT=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_COMMANDS=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_PATHS=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_EDITS=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_WRITES=0` and `DEJA_INCLUDE_SUBAGENTS=0` leave the same records out of an import as out of a local read, and the import says how many (#5425).
Recalled

deja now reads Windsurf / Devin Desktop: Cascade's encrypted conversation
files are decrypted, authenticated and indexed, and `deja install windsurf`
adds the MCP server, a global rule, the skill and a `/deja` workflow. That
makes 42 harnesses. Grok Build installs the plugin from this repository's own
marketplace, and a Spec Kit extension ships with each release. The person sees
more of what deja did: the first session names an error the machine keeps
hitting, the weekly note names the session agents used, and dsh, Hermes,
OpenClaw and Gemini show deja's line where the person reads it. Kimi Code and
Qwen Code edit calls are pinned by fixtures from @beiryu.

`deja delete` and `D` in the TUI erase a session from its agent and from
deja after asking. Claude Code sessions whose transcript is gone come back as
their prompts from `history.jsonl`, and without `zstd` a compressed rollout no
longer makes every search rewrite the index.

### Changed

- deja's lines for the person fit on one line each, and a session start shows the recall receipt plus at most one once-only note (the built note, what changed, the week note, the GitHub line), so a fresh install no longer opens with four lines. The receipt drops its byte count and the docs line folds into the built note. What the model receives is unchanged.

### Added

- `DEJA_THEME=dracula` paints the interactive screen in the Dracula palette, for terminals themed that way. `light` and `dark` work as before, and a name deja does not know still falls back to the terminal background. From @demrom (#5106).
- `deja delete <id>` and `D` in the TUI erase a session from its agent and from deja's index, after asking; there is no undo. `--dry-run` lists the files. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Cline CLI, Kimi Code, Grok, dsh, pi, Senpi, OpenClaw and Antigravity are removed as files, opencode through `opencode session delete`. Running sessions, shared stores and unchecked agents are refused.
- A guide on deleting Copilot CLI session history: find the session by the id in `session.start`, not the directory name, and what `copilot --resume` loses. From @beiryu (#4965).
- A guide on deleting Qwen Code chat history: the chat file, its sub-agent logs, and what `qwen -r` loses. From @beiryu (#4966).
- Claude Code sessions whose transcript is gone come back as their prompts. `~/.claude/history.jsonl` keeps every typed prompt and paste with its session id after the cleanup deletes the transcript, so those sessions are searchable again, filed under the directory they ran in. Only the prompts: `deja show` says so, and `deja resume` refuses one. A session with its transcript on disk, or one deja kept after it was deleted, is left to the transcript. `DEJA_CLAUDE_HISTORY_FILE` moves the file (#5046).
- The guide on deleting old Claude Code sessions in Chinese, with the same commands and numbers: 368 of 1,320 files are older than 30 days and hold 4% of the bytes, while the ten largest hold 86%. From @beiryu (#4970).
- The Claude Code and Cursor memory guides in Chinese, with the same commands and numbers. From @Quartex246 (#5019, #5020).
- The Codex CLI history guide in Chinese: where the rollouts live, why a plain `grep` stops seeing sessions older than a week, the `jq` and `sqlite3` recipes, and search and SSH sync. From @ursasi (#5085).
- Five more guide pages in Chinese, with their commands and paths kept verbatim: deleting Codex sessions, deleting Cursor chats, Codex resume and its two errors, the Claude Code "No conversation found with session ID", and the full context window with its measured 77% / 0.2%. From @ursasi (#5080, #5081, #5082, #5083, #5084).
- Shell completion for `deja recall`: `--project`, `--harness` with the harness names, and `--limit` in bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell, where it used to offer search flags recall refuses. zsh's command list now offers recall too. From @orshih6 (#5015).
- A [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) extension: `/spe

Reading a session back now shows the code it changed, each edit as the lines
it removed and added, for Claude Code, Codex and every harness whose
transcript holds its edit calls. A Codex session opens in the ChatGPT desktop
app with `deja resume <id> --app`, and the screen gets find in a session,
filters in the box and cards that lead with the question. Session start takes
0.38 s instead of 1.46 s and the per-prompt hook 0.59 s instead of 1.65 s on a
19k-session index, and an opencode 2.x store no longer stalls a new session's
first request. Secrets that slipped past redaction are masked, and the index
holds up under crashes and concurrent use. The index version is now 70, so the
store rebuilds once on the first run after upgrading.

### Added

- Reading a session back shows the code it changed, each edit as the lines it removed and added. MCP `recall_context` and the session resource put it ahead of the conversation, `deja ctx` after the digest. Drafts the session rewrote are folded into their final form, the project's code comes before its tests, and the agent's reproduction scripts and notes are left out. On 48 SWE-ContextBench tasks the session that fixed the same code used to arrive with none of its fix; now 14 show most of it. Read from the transcript when asked, so the index stays the same size and keeps the written side as hashes. Claude Code, Codex and any harness whose transcript holds its edit calls as JSON, one session per file (#4935, #4950, #4955).
- `deja resume <id> --app` opens a Codex CLI session in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS and Windows, and the screen's continue picker offers the app first for a Codex session (#4907).
- The screen's cards lead with the question asked, the home list is grouped by day, and dates count calendar days. The preview shows how the session went, turn by turn, with the commands and the files it edited. In the reader `/` finds a word in the session, `n` and `N` step through the matches, `]` and `[` jump between the turns you asked, and `t` unfolds long messages. The box takes filters: an agent with a colon (`codex:`), `today`, `yesterday`, `week`, `month` and `in:<project>`. A search that finds nothing names the other projects that have it, or the spelling your history uses. The Kept tab is now Deleted, headed "Deleted by their agent, kept by deja", and `tab` cycles this project, all projects and Deleted. The continue picker preselects and marks the agent used last and folds agents not installed into one line. `^k` also copies the session id or project path and forgets a session, after asking, and `?` lists every key (#4911).

### Changed

- Reading one session back no longer walks the whole record log: a table beside it says where each session's records are, and the first line of each repeated error is kept at build time. On a 19k-session index session start takes 0.38 s instead of 1.46 s, MCP recall 0.95 s instead of 1.29 s and `deja show` 17% less, for 0.33% more index. A full rebuild there takes about 3 s longer to write the error lines (#4940).
- Hooks answer faster on a large history: on a 19k-session index the per-prompt hook takes 0.59 s instead of 1.65 s and a cold session start 0.74 s instead of 1.42 s, with the same output. Worktrees are listed once per hook instead of once per name lookup, projects are scoped once per name, long sessions are scanned on all cores, and repeated errors are read back in one pass over the record log. The session-start hook runs `git status` without taking the repository's optional lock (#4934).
- Switching tabs on the screen takes 7 ms instead of 46 for this project and 21 instead of 74 for all projects on 27k sessions, and Deleted is instant: the count of every session is read again only after the index changes, and the newest 60 are picked without sorting all of them (#4915).
- The screen's first run shows the index being built: the stage, a bar, each agent ticking in with its session count and the seconds so far, and it lets you in onc

Bare `deja` at a terminal now opens a search screen over every agent's
history: type to search, read a session at the hit, resume it, or carry it
into another agent. It opens on the sessions behind your uncommitted change.
Junie and JetBrains AI Assistant are read, `deja rules sync` writes to 42
agents instead of 8, and recall called by an agent puts the project it works
in first, which took a planted answer from 20 to 43 of 56 real queries. A
transcript its agent deleted no longer makes every search answer stale. The
index version is now 69, so the store rebuilds once on the first run after
upgrading.

### Added

- Bare `deja` at a terminal opens a search screen over every agent's history. Type to search, read a session at the hit, resume it, or carry it into another agent with `ctrl-o`. It opens on the sessions behind your uncommitted change, and on a first run it builds the index behind the screen instead of before it. Pipes, `TERM=dumb` and `DEJA_TUI=0` keep the text summary.
- The first run of a new version says once what it brings: the top three changes in the terminal, one line in the session-start note.
- An empty search in a terminal shows the surprised cat, and the first search that finds something shows the ready one, once per index.
- An interactive command says, at most once a day, when a newer deja release is out, with the upgrade command for whatever installed it (`deja update`, brew, npm, scoop). The look at GitHub runs in a detached process and the next interactive command prints what it found, so no command waits on the network. Hooks, the MCP server, pipes, dev builds, `deja update`, `deja doctor` and `deja version` never start it, and `DEJA_OFFLINE=1` or `DEJA_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE=1` turns it off with no request made (#4622).
- After a search that finds something, in a terminal, deja shows one short tip at most once a day, naming a command you may not have met: `blame`, `fix`, `how` or `view`, in rotation. It goes to stderr and never appears in a pipe, a script, a hook or `--json` (#4629).
- Kimi Code and Kiro get the line about a file before an edit, and CodeWhale the fix pair for a failed command. None of them shows the model what that hook prints, so the line waits for the next hook that does: the next prompt on Kimi and Kiro, the next tool call or message on CodeWhale. CodeWhale also hands over the pre-tool line of a call that failed to run, which it sends back without it.
- `deja resume <id> --write-back` puts a session the agent deleted back where the agent can reopen it, rebuilt from deja's index in the agent's own format. The file holds the user and assistant turns; tool calls and their output stay in deja, which keeps them and reads only what the agent appends later. Works for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, pi, omp, gjc, Kimchi, Senpi, Kimi, Copilot CLI, CodeBuddy, Command Code, CodeWhale, Cline, OpenClaw, Continue, Grok Build and Kiro CLI, each checked by resuming the written file in the real CLI. For agents that keep sessions in a database, or whose format needs something the index lacks, it says what is missing. It never replaces a file and writes only inside the agent's store (#4617).
- aider edits record both sides, read from the SEARCH/REPLACE block, unified diff or patch in the reply once aider says it applied them, so `deja restore` and line-level `deja blame` answer for aider sessions (#595).
- VS Code Copilot Chat edits record the replaced text, read from the edit call's arguments, so `deja restore` and line-level `deja blame` answer for them. On one machine's store that is 638 spans where there were none. The extension's agent transcripts record both sides of an edit and its file (#595).
- Junie and JetBrains AI Assistant are read. Junie gets `junie` and `junie-auto` (hooks, MCP, skill, `/deja`, rules, resume); AI Assistant gets `jetbrains`, the MCP server in `~/.ai/mcp/mcp.json`. Agent chats that run Junie, Claude, Codex or another agent with its own store are left to that store

issues.title: CJK bigrams cost 17.5% of full-build time
edit spans: nineteen readers still record the path without the change line-level blame needs
The agent can reach 6 of deja's 40 commands, and those 6 cost 1915 tokens a session
the pre-tool hook costs 172 ms a call and returns a decision 0 times in 48 on a real store
three quarters of injected blocks carry a mention rather than a conclusion
